title: Chapter 120 — The Deck Towards the End of the First Night Watch
paragraphs: Ahab standing by the helm. Starbuck approaching him.
"We have to send down the main-topsail yard, sir. The band is working loose, and half the strands of the lee lift have parted. Should I strike it, sir?"
"Strike nothing; lash it. If I had sky-sail poles, I'd sway them up now."
"The anchors are working, sir. Shall I get them inboard?"

"Strike nothing and stir nothing, but lash everything down. The wind is rising, but it hasn't reached my tablelands yet. Quick, see to it. — By masts and keels! He takes me for the hunchbacked skipper of some little coasting smack. Send down my main-topsail yard! Ho, you gluepots! The loftiest trucks were made for the wildest winds, and this brain-truck of mine is sailing now among the scudding clouds. Should I strike that? Oh, only cowards send down their brain-trucks in a storm. What a hullabaloo up there! I'd almost take it for the sublime, if I didn't know that colic is a noisy illness. Oh, take some medicine, take some medicine!"
